section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the reward for Torah study is the Garden of Eden, while the reward for mitzvah observance is the Resurrection of the Dead, and that all Jews have a share in the World to Come because they are filled with mitzvos, as indicated by the verse "Your people are all righteous."
section.t: B)
And one point of explanation in this is,
as explained in several discourses,
that the reward of the Garden of Eden is for the occupation with Torah,
and the reward of the Resurrection of the Dead is for the fulfillment of the mitzvos.
And this is that the Garden of Eden is the world of souls
(souls without bodies)
and in the world of Resurrection there will be souls in bodies,
because the occupation with Torah pertains primarily to the soul, and the fulfillment of mitzvos to the body.
And since the fulfillment of mitzvos is in all of Israel,
for even the transgressors of Israel are full of mitzvos like a pomegranate,
therefore all of Israel have a share in the World to Come.
And it may be said,
that this is also what the Mishnah continues with the verse,
"And Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever..."
It may be said,
that the intention of the Mishnah in citing the verse is not only to bring a proof that all of Israel have a share in the World to Come, but also to explain the reason for this.
For one who fulfills mitzvos is called by the name "righteous"
[for all mitzvos are called by the name "tzedakah" (righteousness/charity),
and those who fulfill the mitzvos are called by the name "tzadikim" (righteous ones)],
and since "Your people are all righteous,"
that all of Israel
(even the transgressors among them)
fulfill mitzvos,
and moreover they are full of mitzvos,
for the mitzvos they fulfill fill their entire existence,
therefore "they shall inherit the land forever,"
the land of life,
which refers to the life of the World to Come.
However,
based on this, one must understand why the Mishnah also brings the continuation of the verse, "the shoot of My planting, the work of My hands, in which to take pride,"
for that Israel are "the shoot of My planting" and "the work of the hands" of the Holy One, blessed be He, is from the aspect of their essential existence
(even before they fulfill mitzvos),
and in the Mishnah "All of Israel have a share in the World to Come," it also brings the conclusion of the verse, "the shoot of My planting, the work of My hands, in which to take pride,"
from which it is implied,
that this—that all of Israel have a share in the World to Come—is
(also)
from the aspect of the virtue that is in them from their own essence.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the revelation at the Resurrection of the Dead involves two aspects: the reward for mitzvah observance and the revelation of Israel's essential virtue as "the shoot of My planting," which is the primary innovation of the Resurrection.
section.t: C)
And it may be said,
that in the revelation that will be at the Resurrection of the Dead there are two matters.
The reward for the service of fulfilling mitzvos
(and "Your people are all righteous"),
that the influences that Israel drew down through the mitzvos they fulfilled will then be revealed,
and through this they will ascend
(afterwards)
to a more elevated level,
that the virtue of Israel from their own essence will be revealed,
that they are "the shoot of My planting, the work of My hands, in which to take pride,"
which is a level higher even than the influence drawn down through the fulfillment of mitzvos.
And it may be added,
that the primary innovation and elevation of the Resurrection of the Dead is that then the virtue of Israel themselves will be revealed.
For the revelation of the influence drawn down through the mitzvos,
will also be in the days of Moshiach
(before the time of the Resurrection),
and as explained in Tanya,
that through our actions and service now we draw down the Ein Sof below, and the revelation of this drawing down will be in the days of Moshiach and in the Resurrection of the Dead
(except that in the Resurrection of the Dead,
even the revelation of this drawing down will be in a more elevated manner),
and the primary innovation and elevation of the Resurrection of the Dead is that then the root of Israel will be revealed, as they are rooted in the Awtsmoos.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section clarifies that the reward discussed in earlier discourses refers to the reward for Israel's service in Torah and mitzvos, while the essential innovation of the World to Come is the revelation of Israel's own virtue as "the shoot of My planting."
section.t: And it may be said,
that what is stated in several discourses
(cited above)
that in the Resurrection of the Dead there will be a revelation of the influence drawn down through the fulfillment of mitzvos,
is,
because there it speaks of the reward for Israel that will be in the World to Come for their service in Torah and mitzvos in this world,
and the perfection of the reward is that the influence they drew down through the fulfillment of mitzvos will shine for them in revelation.
And therefore it is explained in these discourses that the reward of souls in the Garden of Eden is that they attain the G-dliness of the Torah they studied in this world,
for Torah is the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He,
the light that fills,
and the reward of the Resurrection of the Dead is that then our eyes will see the revelation of His G-dliness that transcends the worlds,
drawn down through the fulfillment of mitzvos,
His will, blessed be He,
(which is above His wisdom),
the light that surrounds.
However,
all this is the reward for Israel for their service in Torah and mitzvos.
And the primary innovation and elevation that will be in the World to Come is the revelation of the virtue of Israel themselves,
"the shoot of My planting, the work of My hands, in which to take pride."
